crossref.title: Genome-wide polyadenylation site mapping datasets in the rice blast fungus Magnaporthe oryzae
crossref.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>Polyadenylation plays an important role in gene regulation, thus affecting a wide variety of biological processes. In the rice blast fungus <jats:italic>Magnaporthe oryzae</jats:italic> the cleavage factor I protein Rpb35 is required for pre-mRNA polyadenylation and fungal virulence. Here we present the bioinformatic approach and output data related to a global survey of polyadenylation site usage in <jats:italic>M. oryzae</jats:italic> wild-type and <jats:inline-formula><mml:math xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML">
                      <mml:mrow>
                        <mml:mi>Δ</mml:mi>
                      </mml:mrow>
                    </mml:math></jats:inline-formula><jats:italic>rbp35</jats:italic> strains under a variety of nutrient conditions, some of which simulate the conditions experienced by the fungus during part of its infection cycle.</jats:p>

In the rice blast fungus Magnaporthe oryzae the cleavage factor I protein Rpb35 is required for pre-mRNA polyadenylation and fungal virulence.
